title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cross Creek, PA

metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cross Creek, PA | Washington Co
metaDescription: Cross Creek sits in western Washington County's core Marcellus wet-gas country. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly, cash offer, no broker fee.
heroLead: Cross Creek sits in the rural western half of Washington County, where the land is mostly open farmland and the drilling units are some of the more consistently active in the state.
intro: Western Washington County, the stretch that includes Cross Creek and the park that shares its name, has been core wet-gas territory for Range Resources and other operators for well over a decade now. If your family owns land here, there's a decent chance you're already receiving royalty payments, or that a neighbor's unit has already touched your acreage even if your own tract hasn't been drilled yet.
We buy Cross Creek-area mineral and royalty interests directly, and part of what we do before quoting a number is check exactly what's happening on and around your specific parcel.

sections.heading: Core Wet-Gas Ground, Consistently Active
paragraphs: This part of Washington County has drawn sustained operator interest for its liquids-rich Marcellus production, and Cross Creek-area acreage sits well within that footprint. That's a meaningfully different starting point than flank counties where activity is spottier. It doesn't mean every parcel is producing today, but it does mean nearby activity is genuinely relevant to what your interest might be worth.
We pull current permitting and production records for your specific section rather than relying on the county's broad reputation alone.

sections.heading: Cross Creek Park and Surrounding Farmland
paragraphs: The area around Cross Creek Lake and its state park has stayed largely rural, which means a lot of the mineral ownership here is still tied to working farms and family land rather than developed residential lots. That rural character has, if anything, made this ground more attractive to operators looking for larger contiguous drilling units, since farmland assembles into units more easily than subdivided residential parcels do.
If your family's farm has been approached about leasing, or already has an active lease, we can review those terms as part of making you an offer.

sections.heading: Deductions on an Active Unit
paragraphs: Even on a genuinely active unit, post-production deductions can eat into a royalty check more than owners expect, gathering, compression, and marketing costs all coming off before you see a dollar. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act guarantees a one-eighth royalty on the gross, not a deduction-free check. If your Cross Creek-area statement looks lower than you'd expect for active production, we'll go through it with you honestly.

faqs.question: Is the ground around Cross Creek actively drilled?
faqs.answer: This part of western Washington County has been core wet-gas territory for years, though activity still varies parcel to parcel, so we check your specific section.

faqs.question: My family farms this land. Will selling mineral rights interfere with that?
faqs.answer: No. Selling your mineral interest doesn't touch your surface ownership or your ability to keep farming.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check smaller than I expected from an active unit?
faqs.answer: Usually post-production cost deductions, which are legal in Pennsylvania unless your specific lease bars them. Send us your statement and we'll walk through it.
